summary.text: Jeremy Moss is the Democratic nominee for Michigan's 11th District and a Michigan state senator from Southfield. A former Southfield city councilmember and state representative, he has served in the Legislature since 2015, including as Senate President Pro Tem. He is running on healthcare costs, the cost of living and opposition to Trump administration immigration enforcement.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, he is a lifelong Oakland County resident and a graduate of Groves High School; he lives in Southfield.

Earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from Michigan State University. His campaign website says he took part in student humanitarian missions there and then worked under then-Southfield Mayor Brenda Lawrence.
Elected to the Southfield City Council in 2011; his campaign website says he was its youngest-ever member.
Elected to the Michigan House of Representatives (District 35) in 2014 and served from 2015 to 2019.
Won the Michigan Senate seat for District 11 in 2018 and was elected in 2022 to represent District 7, a term that ends in January 2027. He is not seeking re-election to that seat.
In the Senate, chairs the Elections Committee and the Senate Regulatory Reform Committee (2025-2026); earlier terms included chairing the Elections and Ethics Committee.

His campaign website says he led the 2022 effort to win a Democratic Michigan Senate majority and served as Senate President Pro Tem, and that he sponsored the most bills signed into law among state legislators in 2023.
Won the Democratic primary for Michigan's 11th District on August 4, 2026.
